nodes.label: Desktop Release
nodes.rationale: Builds and publishes tagged Windows desktop releases with the web app, server bundle, native Electron modules, and desktop main process.

nodes.label: Historical Differential Asset Normalization
nodes.rationale: Older releases used inconsistent installer and blockmap naming, so the workflow uploads aliases matching the installer name expected by electron-updater.

nodes.label: Differential Update Asset Verification
nodes.rationale: Ensures the release includes both the exact installer blockmap named by latest.yml and the latest.yml updater manifest.

nodes.label: Scoped Subgraph Queries
nodes.rationale: Graphify query, path, and explain commands are preferred because they return smaller, focused subgraphs before broad source browsing.

nodes.label: Incremental Graph Updates
nodes.rationale: After code changes, graphify update keeps the AST-derived project graph current without API cost.

nodes.label: Pet Needs System
nodes.rationale: Hunger, energy, and fun persist across restarts and decay while the user is away, with caps preventing severe weekend starvation.

nodes.label: startFalling
nodes.rationale: A gravity simulation visibly returns a released pet to the desktop or detected platform instead of snapping the window downward.

nodes.label: AFK Sleep
nodes.rationale: The pet sleeps after more than four minutes of keyboard inactivity and wakes when activity resumes.

nodes.label: Offline Capture Queue
nodes.rationale: When TimeBlock is offline, up to 100 captures remain in extension storage and are retried every minute.

nodes.label: Brainclip Privacy Controls
nodes.rationale: Password fields are ignored, sensitive hostnames can be excluded, and automatic copy capture can be paused.

nodes.label: Localhost-Only Delivery
nodes.rationale: Brainclip sends captures to the local TimeBlock server, normally at 127.0.0.1:4141.

nodes.label: Maximum Clip Size Setting
nodes.rationale: Selections are truncated to avoid accidental full-page copies flooding the vault.

nodes.label: Cat Sprite Sheet
nodes.rationale: Twenty-one fully composited 32x32 frames let the renderer move one texture instead of animating individual body parts.
